title: Why a search box shows stale results
purpose: See how two racing fetches cause stale results, and why a breakpoint finds the cause faster than console.log.
sequence_reason: The bug depends on the order in which two responses arrive, so motion shows the cause better than one static picture.
summary: A user types re and then react in a search box. Each input event starts a fetch. The react response arrives first and the slow re response arrives last, so the list shows results for the old query. A breakpoint pauses the code before a line runs, so you can read the Scope, Watch and Call Stack panes instead of guessing with console.log.
explanation: Two requests can be in flight at the same time. The response that arrives last overwrites the list, even when it belongs to an old query.

learning_check.question: Why does the list show results for re when the box says react?
learning_check.answer: The re request was slower. Its response arrived after the react response and overwrote the list.

scenes.heading: Stale search results

scenes.heading: Two requests race
scenes.narration: The user types re, then react. Each input event starts a fetch to the server. The react response comes back first. The slow re response comes back last and overwrites the list.
